audit_meta.title: Full-Stack Project Audit Plan
audit_meta.description: Paste the MASTER PROMPT below into your AI with your project structure to receive a structured JSON audit report + action checklist.

master_prompt:
You are a senior full-stack software architect. I need you to perform a comprehensive project audit on my full-stack codebase. My stack is: React / Next.js (frontend), Node.js / Express (backend), Python / Django or FastAPI (backend services), and PostgreSQL / MySQL / MongoDB (database layer).

I will provide you with:
- My project folder/file structure (paste it below)
- My package.json (frontend and/or backend)
- My requirements.txt or pyproject.toml (Python services)
- Any config files (next.config.js, .env.example, webpack, babel, etc.)

Your job is to analyze the project and return a SINGLE valid JSON object that follows this exact schema. Do not include any explanation outside the JSON.

[PASTE YOUR FOLDER STRUCTURE AND CONFIG FILES BELOW THIS LINE]



[END OF PROJECT FILES]

Respond ONLY with the JSON audit report following this schema exactly.

project_summary.project_name: string — inferred from package.json or root folder name

entry_points: list of main entry files e.g. pages/_app.tsx, src/index.jsx

imports: list of files this file imports
imported_by: list of files that import this file
component_tree.is_leaf: boolean — true if nothing imports this file

external_packages_used: list of npm packages actually used in code
external_packages_declared_but_unused: npm packages in package.json not found in any import

imports: list of files this file imports
imported_by: list of files that import this file

external_packages_used: list of npm packages actually used
external_packages_declared_but_unused: npm packages declared but not imported anywhere

imports: list of modules this file imports
imported_by: list of files that import this file

packages_used: list of pip packages actually used in code
packages_declared_but_unused: packages in requirements.txt not found in any import

orm_models_used: list of models/tables that appear in queries or routes
orm_models_defined_but_unused: models defined but never queried or referenced

files.layer: frontend | backend_node | backend_python | database | config | test | assets
files.reason: string — why this file is considered unused
files.last_import_reference: string or null — last file that referenced this, if any

groups.description: string — what is duplicated or overlapping
files: list of relative paths in this duplicate group

items.layer: frontend | backend_node | backend_python | database | build | devops
items.category: performance | code_quality | security | bundle_size | maintainability | scalability
items.title: string — short title of the optimization
items.suggested_fix: string — concrete recommendation or code pattern to adopt

immediate.action: string — imperative verb phrase describing the task
immediate.reason: string — why this must be done now

safe_delete_manifest.description: Files confirmed safe to delete. Review before executing.
safe_delete_manifest.shell_command: string — a single shell command to delete all listed files, e.g. rm -rf path1 path2 ...

usage_instructions.step_2: Paste it into your AI tool (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, etc.).
usage_instructions.step_3: Append your project folder structure (use: find . -type f | sort) below the prompt.
usage_instructions.step_4: Also append your package.json, requirements.txt, and any config files.
usage_instructions.step_5: Run the prompt. The AI will return a JSON matching the 'output_schema' above.
usage_instructions.step_6: Review 'safe_delete_manifest.shell_command' carefully before running any delete commands.
usage_instructions.tip: To get your folder structure fast, run: find . -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/.git/*' -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' -type f | sort
